$comment: Specs KNOWN to fail an attempt and pass on retry. The point is not to
excuse them — it is to make a NEW flake distinguishable from a long-known
one, because on a green shard the two are byte-identical in the log.
ci.yml's 'Name the failing specs' step annotates a known entry as a
::notice (unchanged) and an UNLEDGERED flake as a ::warning. That split is
deliberate and narrow: the step's own comment records that annotating every
green-run flake as an error was measured on run 35427726541 and reverted,
because a step that cries wolf on every green run is one people learn to
ignore. A warning only on something genuinely new is the opposite of that.
Matching is on SPEC FILE + TITLE SUBSTRING, never a line number: a comment
added above a test moves its line (measured — entity-detail-layout went
from :24 to :51 inside one PR) while the test is unchanged.
Deleting an entry is correct the moment a spec is fixed or removed. The
guard asserts every entry's spec file still exists, so a deleted spec
cannot leave its excuse behind. It cannot assert the flake has stopped —
absence is not observable from one run — so that review is a human one.

flakes.title: asset detail page renders the shell
flakes.reason: The App Router transition is DROPPED, not slow: 424 requests with the last at 2.94s then zero network for 29.4s, screencast pixel-static from 2.65s, and the frame URL is /assets/{id} at the start of the expect and /t/{slug}/assets at the end. Cause unidentified — a timeout raise would not help, and the service-worker storm hypothesis measured INCONCLUSIVE (both arms clean) because the flake did not fire in that CI window.

flakes.title: Tasks row double-click navigates to detail
flakes.reason: Same dropped-transition shape as the entity-detail case and in the same E2E shard, which is what made it usable as that experiment's in-run control. Shares expectRouteTransition with it, but the helper is where the failure is CAUGHT rather than caused — ciso-portfolio shows the shape without using it.

flakes.title: CISO creates a 2nd tenant
flakes.reason: CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-10-07 — this is no longer a timing flake, and if it recurs the timing explanation is spent. The wait after the submit was waitForURL(/\/(?:t|org|no-tenant|tenants)\b/), which matches the page the test is already on (/org/acme-org/tenants/new), so it resolved on the first poll and waited for nothing; the safeGoto that follows then navigated while the create POST was still in flight and the browser aborted it. Measured in the trace of run 37561894805: POST /api/org/acme-org/tenants recorded status -1 (no response at all) and the list rendered '1 tenant linked to this organization'. The ~50% rate on main is the race between the create transaction and the navigation that cancels it, which is what made it look like the ~18s shape this entry used to describe. The spec now waits for the POST response and asserts 201 before navigating. Kept rather than pruned because absence is not observable from one run; prune at review if it has not recurred.

flakes.title: a first visit: the inline script corrects it DURING head parsing
flakes.reason: FIRST PAINT never reported: `expect(log.fcp).not.toBeNull()` at :220. Not a navigation timeout like its siblings here — the instrument itself produced no value, which is the same underlying slowness seen from the measurement side rather than the assertion side. Proven a flake on #1323 run 37456682187: attempt 1 red, attempt 2 green on the IDENTICAL commit 6784a0f44.

flakes.title: task detail header — task.key is copyable via CopyText
flakes.reason: Clicked a task row, `waitForURL(/farm-tasks\/[a-z0-9]+$/)` timed out at 30s having stayed on the list. The SAME task-detail route as the data-table-platform entry above, reached by a single click instead of a double-click — which is why #1329 reads this set as a detail-page first-render shape rather than a per-spec bug. It EXHAUSTED all three attempts on #1323 attempt 1 and then passed cleanly on attempt 2 of the identical commit, so retry-exhaustion does not distinguish a flake from a real break in either direction.

flakes.title: F — read-only invariant: AUDITOR cannot create tenant-level records
flakes.reason: Observed on #1316. A DIFFERENT test from the `G — CISO creates a 2nd tenant` entry above, in the same file: #1329 listed ciso-portfolio :183 and :214 together, and only :214 was ledgered, so :183 was still reading as a NEW flake on every occurrence. Ledgered separately rather than by widening G's title, because a title that matched both would excuse any future test in this file.
